correctness.rationale: A fixed cyclic set of r>0 vertices carries an independent permutation and a directed forest rooted at that set. The reduced complete-graph Laplacian nI−J on the n−r nonroot vertices has determinant r n^(n−r−1), with the empty determinant at r=n giving one. Thus the convolution coefficient is c_r=r! r n^(n−r−1) for r<n, with c_n=n!. The weight-k multiplier is the scalar product of these coefficients with the coefficients of (1−z)^k(1+z)^(n−k). For r=n−1−m≥1, one has v_p(c_r)=b+ma−v_p(m!)+v_p(r), since v_p(n−i)=v_p(i) for 1≤i<n. Legendre's bound v_p(m!)≤(m−1)/2 gives v_p(c_r)≥b+a for m≥1, and ≥b+2a for m≥2 (m=2 directly). For 0<k<n the sole leading term modulo p^(b+a) is c_(n−1)(−1)^k(n−2k), with v_p(n−2k)=v_p(k)<a. At k=n the two terminal terms sum to (n−1)! n(n−2); the r=n−2 Krawtchouk coefficient is −binom(n,2), supplying a further p^a in that term, and all earlier terms are already divisible by p^(b+2a). This proves the boundary valuation b+a, including n=3. The trivial shell counts n^n. The Walsh matrix is invertible over Z_(p) because its square is 2^n I, so diagonalization yields the local Smith factors, exact rank after normalization, and determinant assertion. Every kernel coefficient is divisible by p^b, which also directly proves that the normalization is integral. Independent leaf-pruning and signed summation over all maps gave the shell multipliers (27,−7,−1,−3) at n=3 and (3125,−13,−39,−169,−163,−165) at n=5; recursive polynomial coefficient checks agreed at n=9,25,27,49,81,121,169 as well. These are corroboration, not the proof for all p,a.
residual_risks: At p=2 the Walsh change of basis need not be locally invertible. Non-prime-power dimensions and Smith factors at other primes are not covered.
